title: AI adoption metrics every creative team should track
summary: Which AI adoption metrics show real progress? Learn what creative leaders should track to spot faster workflows, less rework and consistent quality.
body_markdown:
TL;DR


AI licenses don't tell you whether your rollout is working. Treat adoption as the leading indicator and track four layers: how deeply people use AI, how it changes the workflow, whether quality holds and what it contributes to the business. The single best signal is time to first draft, read alongside rework rate, with ROI measured later once the data is in.


**AI has found its way into almost every business. But how much value does it add?**


Nearly[9 in 10 respondents to McKinsey's August 2026 State of AI survey](https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/quantumblack/our-insights/the-state-of-ai) report regular AI use in at least one business function. Yet just 6% qualify as AI high performers, attributing 5% or more of EBIT to AI and seeing significant value, a share unchanged from 2025.


Marketing shows the same gap. CMOs now put an average of[15.3% of marketing budgets into AI](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026-05-11-gartner-2026-cmo-spend-survey-finds-cmos-allocate-15-point-3-percent-of-marketing-budgets-to-ai-but-only-30-percent-are-ready-to-scale-ai-capabilities) , according to Gartner, even though **70% say their internal processes aren't mature enough to implement and scale it effectively.**


Not sure whether AI has become a truly useful part of your creative team's workflow? Then it's time to look closely at your AI adoption metrics. This article unpacks what to track and how to read the numbers.


## Measure AI adoption before you measure ROI


If you've just rolled out a new AI tool, it can take months to get a clear picture of your return on investment. Even then, linking performance changes to AI use isn't always straightforward.


In[Adobe's 2026 AI and Digital Trends report](https://business.adobe.com/resources/digital-trends-report.html) , a survey of 3,000 executives and practitioners in customer experience roles, **52% said their organization struggles to demonstrate measurable returns on AI using CX-related metrics** . Only 44% have a measurement framework for generative AI, and just 31% for agentic AI.


That makes ROI a slow, lagging measure to rely on alone. **Adoption metrics are the leading indicator.** They show up in weeks, and you can act on them right away.


The key is to track usage, speed and quality as the rollout progresses, then assess the financial return once you have enough data.


**This table shows what to measure and how to act on it:**


What you want to know What to track How to use the results


Does my team use AI regularly? Weekly usage and repeat use of specific AI workflows Identify where people need training or where a tool isn't useful


Is AI helping work move faster? Time to first draft, alongside revisions needed before approval Check whether faster drafts save time overall or create extra work later


Is the work still on brand? Share of AI-assisted assets that pass brand review the first time Spot quality problems before you expand AI use


Has it been worth the investment? Financial benefits compared with the full cost of tools, training and implementation Assess ROI once you have enough reliable data


When you reach that last row, our guides to[measuring AI ROI for creative teams](https://www.superside.com/blog/measure-ai-roi-for-creative-teams) and the[ROI of AI creative workflows](https://www.superside.com/blog/roi-ai-creative-workflows) pick up where this article leaves off.


## The four layers of AI adoption measurement


A useful AI adoption measurement framework covers four layers.


### 1. Adoption depth: Measure real AI usage


Start with behavior rather than access. AI usage only becomes meaningful when people return to the tools and build them into their work.


**Here's what to measure, plus the common pitfalls:**


Metric Definition How to measure it Common challenge


Active usage rate Share of the team that uses AI in real work each week Platform usage data Counting licenses as adoption


Usage depth Average number of distinct AI workflows used per person Workflow-level tracking A few heavy users mask low overall adoption


Workflow coverage Share of defined creative workflows with a useful AI step Workflow audit Counting workflows that teams rarely use


Voluntary reuse Share of AI workflows people repeat without prompts or mandates Repeat usage over time Pilot activity inflates the data


Segment the data by workflow and, where useful, by AI feature. A healthy overall usage rate can hide the fact that only one or two use cases have gained real traction.


If the numbers point to skills gaps, our guides to[gen AI training for creative teams](https://www.superside.com/blog/gen-ai-training-for-creative-teams) and[building an AI-ready creative team](https://www.superside.com/blog/building-and-training-ai-powered-creative-team) can help.


### 2. Workflow impact: Connect adoption to delivery


Once people use AI regularly, the next question is whether it changes how work gets done.


**These metrics show where[AI is making a difference](https://www.superside.com/blog/ai-first-companies) :**


Metric Definition How to measure it Common challenge


Share of assets AI touched Percentage of delivered assets that included a substantive AI step Project metadata Counting trivial prompts as meaningful use


Time to first draft Time from creative brief to first reviewable output Project timestamps Faster drafts that lead to more rework


Rework rate Revisions per asset before final approval Review-system data Fewer revisions because quality standards slipped


Review rounds Approval cycles per asset Review-system data Fewer rounds because review became less rigorous


**For creative teams, time to first draft is one of the clearest signs of workflow change.** But read it alongside rework rate and review rounds. A faster first draft that leads to more revisions simply moves the time and cost elsewhere.


A clear[creative brief](https://www.superside.com/blog/creative-briefs-production) also makes this metric more reliable, since a vague brief inflates both draft time and rework.


Also look at where the saved time goes. If AI cuts production time, track whether the team redirects it to higher-value work, because that's where productivity gains start to show up in business outcomes.


### 3. Output quality: Check whether speed comes at a cost


Faster workflows only tell part of the story. Include quality metrics in your AI adoption dashboard from the start, so you can see what happens to the work as AI use grows.


**Here's what to track:**


Metric Definition How to measure it Common challenge


Brand-consistency pass rate Share of AI-assisted assets that pass brand review the first time Review checkpoints Brand standards drift over time


Quality parity AI-assisted and traditional output assessed against the same quality bar Blind review sample Reviewers know which work used AI


Performance parity In-market performance of comparable AI-assisted and traditional assets Campaign analytics Media spend or targeting distorts the comparison


Escalation rate Share of work that needs senior creative intervention Workflow data Informal rescue work goes unrecorded


Why measure these separately? The[Content Marketing Institute's B2B research for 2026](https://contentmarketinginstitute.com/b2b-research/b2b-content-marketing-trends-research-2026) , a survey of 1,015 B2B marketers, found that among those using AI for content creation:


- **87%** say productivity has improved.
- **80%** say operational efficiency has improved.
- **58%** say content quality has improved.
- **39%** say content performance has improved, while **34%** see no change.


The research doesn't say AI caused that gap between productivity and performance. But it shows why productivity, quality and performance each need their own metric.


For practical advice, read our articles on how to[build a creative review workflow](https://www.superside.com/blog/build-creative-review-workflow) and[maintain brand consistency at scale](https://www.superside.com/blog/maintain-brand-consistency-at-scale) .


### 4. Business contribution: Connect adoption to real value


The fourth layer connects what's happening in the creative workflow with the value it creates. You don't need a full ROI calculation yet. Look for signs that workflow changes translate into measurable value.


Metric Definition Common challenge


Creative throughput Assets delivered per period with the same number of people More volume without more useful demand


Content velocity Time from creative brief to in-market Faster delivery of low-priority work


Time redirected Hours moved to higher-value work Claimed savings with no evidence of reallocation


Cost per asset Fully loaded production cost Optimizing only the easiest or cheapest assets


If AI helps a team[produce more work with the same number of people](https://www.superside.com/blog/scale-creative-production-with-ai) , shorten the path from brief to market or reduce cost per asset, it's starting to make a solid contribution.


Time redirected deserves particular attention, because an hours-saved figure on its own tells you very little. **Ask what the team did with that time** . Did people take on more high-value creative work, or respond to other briefs faster?


**Our guide to[creative content velocity](https://www.superside.com/blog/creative-content-velocity) explores how teams increase the speed and volume of production while protecting quality.**


## AI adoption: What not to measure


Some AI metrics make adoption look healthier than it is. **On their own, these three can mislead you:**


- **Licenses issued:** A license shows someone has access to an AI tool. It doesn't tell you whether they use it, how often or whether it's part of their everyday workflow.
- **Hours saved in isolation:** Time savings can support a strong business case, but the number needs context. How credible is the estimate? Where did the time go? And what happened to the quality of the work?
- **Total prompts or generations:** More AI activity doesn't necessarily mean more value. Prompt volume can rise because people struggle to get a usable result, or simply because a pilot requires frequent use. Without an outcome attached, volume tells you very little.


[Deloitte's October 2026 State of AI in the Enterprise report](https://www.deloitte.com/us/en/what-we-do/capabilities/applied-artificial-intelligence/content/state-of-ai-in-the-enterprise.html) , based on a survey of 3,500 senior leaders across 25 countries, shows why outcomes matter more than activity.


**74% report efficiency and productivity gains from AI** and 45% report cost reductions, yet only 28% are realizing revenue gains.


## AI adoption rate benchmarks worth tracking


Benchmarks show where your team's AI adoption sits relative to other organizations.


Each study measured a different audience, behavior or definition of adoption, so treat these figures as reference points rather than targets.


**Every figure carries its sample:**


Benchmark Finding Sample Source


Regular AI use in at least one business function Nearly 9 in 10 1,719 respondents in 97 countries McKinsey, Aug. 2026


AI high performers (5% or more of EBIT from AI) 6% 1,719 respondents in 97 countries McKinsey, Aug. 2026


Marketing leaders with mature AI readiness 30% 401 CMOs and senior marketing leaders Gartner, May 2026


Average marketing budget allocated to AI 15.3% 401 CMOs and senior marketing leaders Gartner, May 2026


Struggle to show AI returns using CX metrics 52% 3,000 CX executives and practitioners Adobe, 2026


Have a generative AI measurement framework 44% 3,000 CX executives and practitioners Adobe, 2026


Realizing revenue gains from AI 28% 3,500 senior leaders in 25 countries Deloitte, Oct. 2026


Marketing leaders using AI in everyday creative work 97% 1,415 marketing leaders at companies with 500+ employees Canva and The Harris Poll, 2026


Enterprise leaders using gen AI at least weekly 82% (46% daily) Enterprise business leaders Wharton and GBK Collective, Oct. 2025


Creative teams with AI fully integrated into workflows 2% 190 creative leaders Superside


(Sources:[McKinsey](https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/quantumblack/our-insights/the-state-of-ai) ,[Gartner](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026-05-11-gartner-2026-cmo-spend-survey-finds-cmos-allocate-15-point-3-percent-of-marketing-budgets-to-ai-but-only-30-percent-are-ready-to-scale-ai-capabilities) ,[Adobe](https://business.adobe.com/resources/digital-trends-report.html) ,[Deloitte](https://www.deloitte.com/us/en/what-we-do/capabilities/applied-artificial-intelligence/content/state-of-ai-in-the-enterprise.html) ,[Canva](https://www.canva.com/newsroom/news/marketing-ai-report-2026/) ,[Wharton](https://knowledge.wharton.upenn.edu/special-report/2025-ai-adoption-report/) and[Superside](https://www.superside.com/blog/ai-adoption-trends-what-creative-leaders-said) )


The headline numbers are high.[Canva and The Harris Poll's State of Marketing and AI 2026](https://www.canva.com/newsroom/news/marketing-ai-report-2026/) found that **97% of marketing leaders use AI in their everyday creative work** , and 89% save at least four hours a week.


The pace of adoption is striking too. The[Wharton and GBK Collective 2025 AI Adoption Report](https://knowledge.wharton.upenn.edu/special-report/2025-ai-adoption-report/) found that weekly gen AI use among enterprise leaders rose from 37% in 2023 to 72% in 2024 and 82% in 2025, with 46% using it daily.


**Zoom in on creative teams, though, and the picture changes.** Superside's survey of[190 creative leaders](https://www.superside.com/blog/ai-adoption-trends-what-creative-leaders-said) found that 52% were still exploring or experimenting, 30% used AI regularly and only 2% had fully integrated AI into their creative workflows.


Our[Breakpoint report](https://www.superside.com/blog/breakpoint) also found that creative teams' success metrics remain rooted in productivity and efficiency rather than value.


So where should your team sit? There's no magic percentage. These benchmarks give context, but your own data tells you more. Establish a baseline, then track how usage, workflow integration, quality and business contribution change over the next six months.


## How to read the numbers for success


**A few simple rules keep your AI adoption dashboard honest:**


- **Pair speed with quality:** Read time to first draft alongside rework, review rounds and quality metrics. A faster draft loses its shine if it creates more work later.
- **Segment by workflow:** Team-wide averages hide a lot. One workflow may be part of everyday work while another was abandoned after the pilot.
- **Track the trend over time:** Early curiosity can quickly boost usage and active user counts. What matters more is whether people come back and adoption grows.
- **Define each metric upfront:** Decide what counts as an AI-touched asset, an active user and a successful workflow before you collect data. Clear definitions make comparisons useful.
- **Keep the comparison fair:** Compare work produced from similar briefs, against the same quality standards and under similar conditions.
- **Check how audiences respond:** For customer-facing work, track feedback, engagement and campaign results alongside internal quality checks. Work can pass brand review and still fall flat.


## What a healthy AI adoption curve looks like


[AI adoption](https://www.superside.com/blog/ai-adoption-creative-teams) rarely rises steadily. A training session may prompt a burst of experimentation, followed by a dip as the novelty fades and people work out which uses are worth keeping.


**A dip at week six isn't failure. A flat line at month six is.**


**What happens after that first burst matters most** . Do team members return to AI workflows that solve real problems? Do they use them without reminders? Have those workflows become part of everyday production?


A drop in total usage can be healthy if people have dropped unhelpful experiments and settled on a few reliable workflows. But if they stop using AI altogether, or only use it when required, ask why.


They may need more training, clearer guidance or **help with many[other barriers to adoption](https://www.superside.com/blog/barriers-to-ai-adoption-creative-teams) .**


Track repeat use alongside the range of workflows where AI helps. The goal is steady progress in the work your team needs to do, with speed and quality checks to confirm that AI makes a real difference.


## Your first 90 days of AI measurement (Guide)


**If you're[introducing AI into a creative team](https://www.superside.com/blog/introducing-ai-into-a-creative-team) , you don't need the full framework on day one.**


Build it in stages, so each new metric has a clear purpose:


### Days 1 to 30: Establish the baseline


You need a clear picture of where you started before you can measure what changed. Capture baseline figures for time to first draft, review rounds per asset, rework rate and brand-consistency pass rate before AI use becomes widespread.


Define your terms now too. What counts as an AI-touched asset? What makes someone an active user? Which AI uses count as a meaningful part of the workflow?


We took a similar approach with a[Fortune 500 company](https://www.superside.com/blog/fortune-500-ai-strategy) . We started with an AI readiness assessment, mapped 15 high-impact AI use cases and built a prioritized adoption roadmap. **The work identified 25% efficiency gains in selected creative workflows.**


### Days 31 to 60: Measure workflow integration


Now add time to first draft and rework rate to the dashboard, and record which specific AI workflows people use. Look at usage frequency and depth too.


Ask: Does a workflow attract repeat use after the first trial? Do people come back to it without a prompt? These patterns tell you much more than overall usage.


### Days 61 to 90: Add quality and business outcomes


Add brand-consistency pass rate and a blind quality comparison between AI-assisted and traditional output. Where it makes sense, bring in customer feedback and[creative performance metrics](https://www.superside.com/blog/what-is-creative-performance) .


**By day 90, you should be able to answer three questions with data:**


- What share of relevant assets had a substantive AI contribution?
- Did AI reduce time to first draft without increasing rework?
- Did creative quality and[brand consistency](https://www.superside.com/blog/brand-consistency-enterprises) hold?


Those answers give you a much stronger foundation for the next stage, when you connect AI adoption to cost savings, ROI and wider business outcomes.

Track those changes consistently, and you'll know where to offer support, which workflows to expand and which experiments to leave behind. As the evidence builds, you can assess the financial impact.

## FAQs


AI adoption metrics (or AI adoption KPIs) measure whether people use AI in real work and whether that use changes workflows, quality or business outcomes. For creative teams, useful metrics include active usage, usage depth, workflow coverage, time to first draft, rework rate, brand-consistency pass rate, creative throughput and time redirected to higher-value work.


No single metric works for every team, but time to first draft is a strong workflow indicator when paired with rework rate. A faster first draft only helps if your team doesn't pay for that speed with extra revisions or lower-quality output.


Hours saved are useful, but they don't tell the whole story on their own. Estimates are often self-reported, and they don't show whether quality held or whether the freed-up time produced more valuable work. Pair them with rework, output quality, throughput or evidence of where the time went.


There's no universal target, because not every creative workflow benefits equally from AI. Rather than chase a headline percentage, track whether adoption grows in the workflows where AI adds value and whether people keep using those workflows over time.


Use explicit quality metrics. Track first-pass brand consistency, compare AI-assisted and traditional work against the same standards, monitor in-market performance and record the share of work that needs senior creative intervention. That shows whether productivity improves while quality holds.


Adoption is the leading indicator: it shows within weeks whether people use AI and whether it changes the work. ROI is the lagging indicator, measured over quarters once you can connect those changes to cost and revenue. Track adoption first, then use it to build your[AI ROI case](https://www.superside.com/blog/measure-ai-roi-for-creative-teams) .
